external_entities.name: supplier
external_entities.description: Suppliers upload compliance paperwork and sign in to the portal.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers sign in with a username and password that the vendor issues to them.

external_entities.name: category manager
external_entities.description: Category managers review uploaded paperwork and approve or reject it from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

external_entities.name: vendor
external_entities.description: The vendor hosts the portal platform and pushes nightly supplier data extracts.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

processes.name: supplier document portal
processes.description: A vendor-hosted SaaS portal through which suppliers upload compliance paperwork and category managers review and approve or reject it.
processes.notes: The vendor's datasheet says the platform is secure by design, that it uses enterprise-grade encryption throughout, that all access is fully authenticated and audited, and that the product is fully compliant.

processes.name: supplier master service
processes.description: A service in the cloud account that loads the nightly supplier extract and writes records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket in the organisation's cloud account where the vendor places the nightly supplier data extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_stores.notes: The runbook for the landing bucket says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_stores.name: supplier database
data_stores.description: The database in the organisation's cloud account into which the supplier master service writes supplier records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A supplier signs in to the supplier document portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers sign in with a username and password that the vendor issues to them.

data_flows.name: upload paperwork
data_flows.description: A supplier uploads compliance paperwork to the supplier document portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.
data_flows.data_description: insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for supplier staff

data_flows.name: review paperwork
data_flows.description: A category manager reviews uploaded paperwork and approves or rejects it in the supplier document portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.
data_flows.data_description: uploaded compliance paperwork and approval or rejection decision

data_flows.name: push supplier extract
data_flows.description: The vendor pushes a nightly supplier data extract to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: The source says the nightly extract is encrypted end to end, while the runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is. These are incompatible claims, so encryption in transit is unknown.

data_flows.name: load extract
data_flows.description: The supplier master service loads the nightly supplier data extract from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file

data_flows.name: write records
data_flows.description: The supplier master service writes supplier records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database

trust_boundaries.name: vendor hosting
trust_boundaries.description: The vendor-controlled hosting environment for the SaaS portal.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier document portal presents a web interface because the source describes it as a portal.
assumptions.basis: The source names the system as a supplier document portal, and portals present web interfaces.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket contains confidential data because the supplier extract contains supplier information, including personal contact details.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the bucket receives a supplier data extract, and the described supplier paperwork includes contact details for staff.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier database contains confidential data because it stores supplier records derived from the supplier extract.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the supplier master service writes supplier records into the database, and the supplier data includes staff contact details.
